* fix: xml root element, root arrays and allOf composition

- Name the document element after the root schema's xml.name, with its
  prefix and namespace, also when the object has a single property (as in
  the OpenAPI 3.2 `<document>` examples).
- Stop splitting unnamed scalar array items into one element per
  character, keep several unnamed root items under one root element and
  treat nullable or untyped arrays as arrays.
- Merge $refs composed in an allOf into one element; keep a single
  (optionally annotated) $ref named like a plain $ref.
- Render oneOf/anyOf properties whose first variant is an inline object,
  a composed allOf or a scalar as their own element.
- Strip skipped readOnly/writeOnly properties nested under a $ref wrapper
  in an allOf instead of throwing.
- Wrap root scalar samples in a root element.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01117LuacuBxMJUn1wJkfdyL

* test: cover the xml root, root array, allOf and oneOf fixes

Six existing nodeType snapshots now include the root element named by the
root schema's xml.name, matching the corresponding examples in the
OpenAPI 3.2 specification (`<document>…</document>`).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01117LuacuBxMJUn1wJkfdyL

* fix: annotated refs with xml, composed arrays and root example arrays

From a review of the XML fixes:

- An allOf of a single $ref that adds its own xml or properties is merged
  and named by the schema, instead of nesting the $ref's element inside it.
- A composed allOf that samples as an array is no longer wrapped twice.
- isArraySchema uses inferType, the type resolution sampling uses, so a
  property typed ['string', 'array'] is no longer dropped.
- A root composed allOf without xml.name is named after its first $ref
  (its xml.name, prefix and namespace, or the component name).
- Root example arrays produce one well-formed document element, including
  with a namespace and for wrapped arrays.
- Repeated root elements are always kept under one root element; two
  existing snapshots that produced two document elements now wrap them.
- Tests: the cases above, unwrapped nullable and untyped property arrays,
  the issue #140 PatchUser + skipReadOnly case, the root null throw, a
  null-first oneOf, nested and additionalProperties arrays, and unit tests
  for stripSkipped, isArraySchema and isAnnotatedRef. 205 tests, 73
  snapshots; JSON output unchanged.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01117LuacuBxMJUn1wJkfdyL

them in one root element).

and additionalProperties arrays. Two existing snapshots that produced two
document elements now wrap them in one root element, as XML 1.0 requires.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01117LuacuBxMJUn1wJkfdyL

* fix: address review on xml root, literal arrays and allOf composition

- Share $ref resolution (resolveRef, with #224 sibling merging) between
  traverse() and the XML root naming; drop the duplicate lookup and catch.
- A root $ref is named once by traverse(), from the $ref and its siblings.
- stripSkipped copies instead of writing to spec objects, so frozen specs
  work and examples are never modified.
- example/default arrays on properties name their items like sampled arrays
  (items xml.name or $ref, else the property name) instead of <0>, <1>.
- Root example arrays name $ref items after the $ref.
- allOf/oneOf with their own example, default, const or enum render as an
  element instead of being dropped.
- Move prefixed/withNamespace to utils and reuse them; trim comments and
  the changeset.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01117LuacuBxMJUn1wJkfdyL

* fix: allOf-wrapped and itemless arrays, unresolvable $refs under examples, composed array items

Found in a second independent review of the previous push:
- An example array under an allOf (e.g. allOf: [$ref] next to xml, the 3.0
  way to annotate a $ref) rendered <0>/<1>: it is now named like other
  literal arrays. An array $ref in a composed allOf keeps its own nodes.
- A $ref under an example or default is never resolved by traverse(), so it
  can be missing or external: refXml now returns null for those instead of
  throwing, and the element falls back to the property name or root.
- A null or scalar value of an array property keeps its element, as on main.
- Composed allOf items of a root array are named after their first $ref
  instead of being merged into one element.
- Arrays without `type: "array"` keep the element nodeType the spec gives
  them (as on main); only the root naming uses the sampled type.
- Tidy: one import line from utils in traverse.js, shorter destructuring.
